versions.mechanism: Waypoints._get_index clamps with max(len-1, min_index) -> ALWAYS returns the LAST waypoint of the list instead of the first waypoint >= min_distance (5 m). Used by PID steering (get_angle), PID target speed (get_target_speed) and World.stop_for_agents (get_vector/get_angle -> obstacle angle frame).
versions.expected_pre_behaviour: Steering look-ahead = last planner waypoint (~10 m ahead at steady state, because the behaviour planner's goal sits ~10 m ahead with the dense 1 m route) instead of ~5 m; obstacle-angle reference vector points to the same far waypoint. On a straight lane: slower lateral convergence; on curves: corner cutting. Target speed unaffected (uniform per message).
versions.covering_note: Mechanism is template-independent (fires every control tick); expected effect WEAK on a mostly-straight lane - look for lateral deviation on the curved segment, not collisions. No clean negative control; use the difftrace (idx differs every tick) as deployment proof.
versions.predicted_metric: off-lane / lateral deviation (weak); no collision predicted
versions.difftrace_var: index returned by Waypoints._get_index inside get_vector (fix: first idx with dist>=5 m; version: len-1)

versions.direction: forward chronology: _get_index as it was BEFORE 793b0c2 (min-clamp; raises ValueError when no waypoint is >= min_distance)
versions.mechanism: Pre-793b0c2 code: wp_index = min(len-1, min_index); when no waypoint is >= 5 m away min_index=-1 -> ValueError('No more waypoints'). 4891c00's fix instead returns the last waypoint. (793b0c2 bug state is v_wp_index; the pre-state DIFFERS from the fix, so this is a distinct version.)
versions.expected_pre_behaviour: Identical to base except when ALL waypoints in the planner list are < 5 m from the ego: then World.stop_for_agents returns speed 0 and the PID brakes (both catch ValueError). Happens for ~4 ticks at route start (ego is stationary anyway) and in the final ~5 m before the route goal.
versions.covering_note: Needs all remaining waypoints within 5 m: only the last 5 m of the route (if the scenario is not terminated earlier by the leaderboard completion radius). Likely inert in our suite.
versions.predicted_metric: stuck in last 5 m (route completion), otherwise none
versions.difftrace_var: index returned by _get_index inside get_vector ('ValueError' string in version when it raises)

versions.direction: revert fix (swap are_on_same_lane argument order in the predicted-trajectory check, stop_person + stop_vehicle)
versions.mechanism: World.stop_person/stop_vehicle: when the obstacle's CURRENT location is not on the ego lane, the fallback checks whether ANY predicted location is on the ego lane via HDMap.are_on_same_lane(a, b). The function is asymmetric only in the junction rule: 'if waypoint_a.is_junction and not waypoint_b.is_junction: return False' (different road_id case). Fixed order (ego, pred): ignore obstacle when EGO is in the junction and the predicted point is outside. Bug order (pred, ego): ignore obstacle when the PREDICTED point is in the junction and the ego is outside -> an approaching ego ignores traffic crossing inside the junction.
versions.expected_pre_behaviour: Ego approaching a junction ignores a vehicle/person whose predicted path lies inside the junction (no braking) -> collision risk; conversely, while inside a junction it brakes for off-junction obstacles on other roads it should ignore.
versions.covering_note: Fires ONLY if road_id differs AND exactly one of (ego, predicted point) is in a junction: i.e. the Crossing vehicle must cross at a junction. Mid-block crossing (same road_id, or off-road -> no DRIVING waypoint) is symmetric -> inert. LeadDecel/LeadStopped: same lane -> fallback never evaluated. Oncoming: same road, different lane_id -> symmetric. CutIn: adjacent lane, same road -> symmetric.
versions.predicted_metric: collision with crossing vehicle (approach phase); unnecessary braking inside junction
versions.difftrace_var: 'ignore <label> <id>' event emitted when the fallback decides to ignore an obstacle (same statement at both call sites)
versions.expected_effect_size: moderate if Crossing is at a junction, else inert

versions.mechanism: World.stop_traffic_light, American-style branch (height_delta > 4): fixed code forces speed_factor_tl=0 when dist_to_intersection<12 and (bbox is None OR bbox area>400). Version: requires bbox area > 400 (would raise AttributeError when bbox is None, i.e. on the --simulator_traffic_light_detection path). Only the world.py hunk is re-expressed; 02c8034's ERDOSAgent visible-TL filter now lives in ERDOSBaseAgent.send_perfect_detections (moved by 52b8570) and its max_angle /4->/3 tweak is not re-expressed.

versions.covering_note: Unreachable in our suite: lights frozen GREEN -> stop_traffic_light returns (True, 1) before this code; the hunk is inside the American-style branch (height_delta>4) which Town01 pole lights do not satisfy; and bbox is None only with --simulator_traffic_light_detection, which neither conf sets.
versions.predicted_metric: none in suite (crash/no-control on perfect-TL path with red light elsewhere)
versions.difftrace_var: speed_factor_tl per traffic light after the style-specific logic (tl id, state, bbox_none, american, dist)

versions.direction: revert the _num_ticks_stopped (>10 ticks) hunk in World.update; ERDOSAgent TL delta_y hunk untouched (now in ERDOSBaseAgent)
versions.mechanism: World.update: fixed code resets _distance_since_last_full_stop / _last_stop_ego_location only after >10 consecutive ticks with forward_speed<0.7 (a genuine full stop). Version resets on the FIRST slow tick. Consumer: stop_for_agents uncontrolled-junction rule (--stop_at_uncontrolled_junctions=True in challenge.conf): speed_factor_stop=0 when a junction is <=13 m ahead, no semaphorized (detected+obeyed) TL, and >13 m driven since last full stop. The unused __init__ line 'self._num_ticks_stopped = 0' is kept so the difftrace is valid in both trees.
versions.expected_pre_behaviour: At a junction that the planner treats as uncontrolled (no TL detected within range), the version 'stops' for a single tick and rolls through; base holds a >10-tick (~0.5 s game time) full stop.
versions.covering_note: Requires a junction within 13 m on the ego route AND no detected/obeyed TL (all Town01 junctions are signalised; frozen-GREEN lights that the camera TL detector sees count as semaphorized -> rule skipped). Fires only on TL-detection misses near a junction. Likely inert; Crossing is the only template whose geometry could matter.
versions.predicted_metric: collision with crossing traffic at junction (less stopping); otherwise none
versions.difftrace_var: World._num_ticks_stopped and _distance_since_last_full_stop at the end of World.update (version: ticks stays 0; dist resets one tick earlier)
versions.expected_effect_size: small (0.5 s shorter stop) and conditional

versions.direction: re-enable OVERTAKE special case in PlanningOperator with pre-commit threshold 35 s (cost_functions 50000->35000 ms)
versions.mechanism: Behaviour planner FSM (live at base) switches FOLLOW_WAYPOINTS->OVERTAKE after the ego has not moved (speed<0.7) for >threshold ms game time, and back after 3 s of motion. Base: PlanningOperator ignores the state (branch commented out) -> stop_for_agents always applied, ego stays stopped. Version: in OVERTAKE the planner runs FOTPlanner.run (Frenet planner over world.waypoints with predicted obstacle corners, max_road_width_l=5 m) and SKIPS stop_for_agents (ignores obstacles/TL speed factors); threshold 35 s instead of 50 s. Two hunks, one mechanism (branch + its threshold). 7be3b0e's behaviour-planner prune hunk is NOT revertable (lines rewritten by ab5384a/793b0c2/47ff456) and is a no-op at base (10 m in both branches).
versions.expected_pre_behaviour: After ~35 s stuck behind a stopped lead, the ego pulls out around it on an FOT path (up to 5 m left = fully into the oncoming lane in Town01), ignoring stop logic for ~3 s of motion, then snaps back to lane following with stop_for_agents -> side-swipe / collision with lead or oncoming, or off-lane excursion; if FOT fails it sends an emergency stop (same as base). Base: stuck behind the lead until timeout.
versions.covering_note: Needs ego stopped (speed<0.7) for >35 s of GAME time: LeadStopped (ego halts behind the lead) and LeadDecel only if the lead ends fully stopped for that long. Scenario must run long enough (>~45 s after the halt). CutIn/Oncoming/Crossing: ego never stuck -> negative controls.
versions.predicted_metric: collision (lead or oncoming) / off-lane; base outcome = stuck
versions.difftrace_var: PlanningOperator state + output waypoint count + first target speed per tick (state OVERTAKE appears 15 s earlier; FOT output replaces follow_waypoints output)
versions.expected_effect_size: strong when it fires; direction is stuck->moving-with-risk, so define the regression metric as collision/off-lane, not stuck

versions.direction: revert ONLY --target_speed 6->7 in challenge.conf (conf-file variant, not source); behaviour-planner prune 2->3 and Dockerfile hunks dropped
versions.mechanism: PlanningOperator (waypoint mode): target_speed = speed_factor * FLAGS.target_speed every tick; PID tracks it. Higher cruise speed with unchanged distance-based stop thresholds (vehicle_max_distance 18 m, coast_factor 1.75, person zones).
versions.expected_pre_behaviour: Cruise at 7 m/s instead of 6: longer stopping distance, later effective braking relative to the fixed distance thresholds -> more/closer rear-end and crossing conflicts.
versions.covering_note: Template-independent (every tick). Strongest expected in LeadDecel/LeadStopped/CutIn/Crossing; Oncoming weakest (opposite-lane vehicle is ignored by the same-lane filter). Deploy by pointing TEAM_CONFIG at <vid>/pylot/simulation/challenge/challenge.conf (the file in the image is otherwise identical).
versions.difftrace_var: FLAGS.target_speed, speed_factor and target_speed per planner tick

versions.direction: revert the __get_goal_location hunk (goal = route[1] always, instead of route[0] when ego is >=5 m from route[0]). NOTE: this hunk is in 793b0c2, NOT in ab5384a as listed in the brief (ab5384a only refactored the goal code into __get_goal_location without changing route[1])
versions.mechanism: BehaviourPlanningOperator.__get_goal_location: the goal (end of the map-computed waypoint list handed to the planner) is route[0] when the ego is >=5 m from it, else route[1]. Route = dense 1 m leaderboard world-coord plan (used since 2019); remove_waypoint_if_close(10) pops one route point per tick, so route[0] settles ~10 m ahead and the goal is ~10 m ahead (base) vs ~11 m ahead (version).
versions.expected_pre_behaviour: Planner waypoint list extends 1 m further; identical lane geometry on a straight road. Differences only where route[0] and route[1] lie on different roads/lanes (junction turns) or at the route end.
versions.covering_note: With a 1 m-spaced route the goal moves by one metre; on a straight lane this is inert. Kept as requested; expect identical outcomes with a trivially different difftrace (goal x,y shifted ~1 m).
versions.difftrace_var: route length, distance to route[0] and the selected goal location per behaviour-planner tick
